research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10045 at 14 FR 1227 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed March 15, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the March 18, 1949 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 2034 to 2876 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier's two spans begin at the heading and then run on into unrelated page text after the order ends. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10045 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy for Emergency Board No. 71 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10045_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10045_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_40f7c1ee3a.txt, a held text lead taken from a scan's text layer and not an authenticated original) is the board's report to the President. Its cover is dated April 6 (the text layer garbles the year digits; the board was appointed March 15, 1949 by this order), and its transmittal letter to the President, dated at St. Louis on April 6 and signed by the board's chairman and two members, submits the board's report as an emergency board designated under Executive Order 10045. The report recites that the board, at the parties' request, stood by until April 4, 1949, when the parties appeared in open session and reported full, complete and final disposition and settlement of all matters in dispute, evidenced by a written agreement signed on April 4, 1949; it therefore reports a settlement and makes no recommendations on the merits. The board's report to the President is accordingly dated April 6, 1949 (the date the parties reported settlement was April 4, 1949), and the standstill, which ran until thirty days after that report, ran to about May 6, 1949. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C) the report deadline and the standstill are not ends: the order was functionally spent on April 6, 1949, when the board made its report, and its standstill period lapsed about thirty days later. It stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering this passage, so it is stated here and not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet locates earlier unfiled versions of this claim in another batch folder; independent review rejected them before filing (a defect in the description of the board's report, now corrected). They were read as drafts and not as evidence; no canonical claim, status hold or conflicting version exists for this order. research_rationale: Executive Order 10083 (14 FR 6161 (Federal Register of October 12, 1949)) was signed October 10, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence beginning “NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 1 of the said International Organizations Immunities Act, I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” and revoking those three orders only so far as they pertain to the three named organizations. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on October 10, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search and the eCFR citation search report no hit naming this order. The packet's U.S. Code search entry also reports no hit, but the current-law table (jobs/current-law/output/ORDERS_CURRENT_LAW.csv) records one U.S. Code mention of this order (usc_mentions 1; MENTIONS.csv row usc:e410b86bce7b): the editorial note to 22 U.S.C. 288 headed 'Public International Organizations Formerly Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges, Exemptions, and Immunities' lists this order as the revoking order for the designations of the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees in the part of the note the held excerpt shows (the table counts three occurrences of the order's number). That note reports the revocation as completed, with the date and Federal Register citation of this order (October 10, 1949, 14 F.R. 6161), and neither restores, extends nor ends anything; it is consistent with the end date recorded here. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.

research_rationale: Executive Order 10084 (14 FR 6245 (Federal Register of October 14, 1949)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10084 was signed October 12, 1949 and takes effect October 1, 1949. Its sole paragraph adopts and prescribes the existing regulations under the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942, and existing departmental regulations and determinations, so far as applicable and appropriate, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Act, and its last sentence reads “This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949, and shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950”. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Effective dates are read as follows. Executive Order 10098 and Executive Order 10118 state no effective date and are recorded as effective on their signing dates, January 25, 1950 and March 27, 1950, which fall before the January 31, 1950 and March 31, 1950 sunsets they restate, so each replaced the sunset then running. Executive Order 10136 (effective July 1, 1950) takes effect the day after June 30, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10118 continued the listed sections. Executive Order 10158 (effective September 1, 1950) takes effect the day after August 31, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10136 continued section 206, but before September 30, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10136 continued section 302, so for section 302 it replaced the September 30 date with October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (effective November 1, 1950) takes effect the day after October 31, 1950. Only Executive Orders 10136 and 10174 take effect after the date they extend. The stated end dates are read inclusively; the exclusive reading would end each continuation when its stated day begins. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

research_rationale: EO 10514 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10514.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier split the order into a lead clause and a stray clause holding only the last year of the effective-date sentence; I replace them with one clause (characters 3415 to 3970 of the registered file), which holds the whole order: under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305) and on the Secretary of the Interior's recommendation, it revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 (hospital-service regulations for the construction and operation of the Government railway in Alaska, now the Alaska Railroad), and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. First end: the revocation is a one-time act and was performed when the order was issued, so the clause was spent on signing, January 19, 1954; the filing date, January 20, 1954 (10:29 a.m.), is the alternative reading. The effective-date sentence makes the revocation of Executive Order 2414 effective retroactively at the close of business on December 31, 1953. That fixes when Executive Order 2414 is treated as ceasing; it cannot fix when this order's own command was performed, because this order did not exist on that date, so December 31, 1953 is the end of the revoked order and not of this one. The consequence, that Executive Order 2414 no longer applies, is a completed result and not a continuing command. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10514 found only the order's own copies, the earlier orders printed in the same issue and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

research_rationale: EO 11332 (March 7, 1967, signed by the President as printed at 32 FR 3877), read in full in the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11332.txt (machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, graded original_representation_unverified and counted as an official original; I did not inspect the PDF page images). The held-text search also returns the capture file for EO 11331, which holds the same Federal Register pages (PDF page 11 of 64) and so contains this order as page text; it is not a later order. Identity: the number, subject and date in the held text agree with the census register. Content: a single operative paragraph. Under section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 and section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, it orders that any income, excess-profits, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1947 to 1968, inclusive, shall, during the Ninetieth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government; the inspection is to follow the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133; and the order takes effect on filing for publication in the Federal Register. First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Ninetieth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1967 to January 3, 1969. Section 1 of the Twentieth Amendment ends the terms of Senators and Representatives at noon on January 3; its text is not held in this packet and the end date is taken from it as a matter of constitutional law. The end is recorded as 1969-01-03, the last day of the Congress, inclusive; the alternative reading is that the Congress ends at noon on that day. No held source lists the session dates of the 90th Congress (the held House Historian capture covers only the 80th to 89th Congresses), so no earlier candidate date is asserted. Later events: none found. The machine searches selected below (U.S. Code, eCFR and the Federal Register order catalog) have no hit for this order. I also read the held text of EO 12553 (51 FR 7237) and its table of revoked orders does not print the number 11332. A general later revocation would in any case fall after the own-terms end. The order is read as terminated at the cutoff 2026-10-14 by its own terms; the standing disclosure that this order rests on a Federal Register OCR text layer and not on an authenticated original applies.

research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 1223, the issue of January 25, 1969) is Executive Order 11452, Establishing the Council for Urban Affairs, dated January 23, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: Executive Order 11541 section 2(b), effective July 1, 1970 under its section 3, which terminates the Council for Urban Affairs by naming this order; this is an earlier end than the provisional status's express revocation by Executive Order 12553 (1986-02-25), which is recorded as a later event. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code search found editorial notes (under 42 U.S.C. 3531 and 31 U.S.C. 501) that recite both the termination by Executive Order 11541 and the revocation by Executive Order 12553, which I read as leads and did not rely on for the ending.
savings_reason: Executive Order 11541, read in full (3,633 characters), has one saving provision, section 1(b), which keeps outstanding delegations, rules, regulations, orders, circulars, bulletins and other executive or administrative action issued or taken by or relating to the Bureau of the Budget or its Director in force, until amended or revoked, as if they related to the Office of Management and Budget. That provision is limited to Bureau of the Budget actions and does not reach the Council for Urban Affairs or this order. Section 2(b) terminates the listed organizations, including the Council for Urban Affairs, outright and provides that their functions are to be performed by the Domestic Council; it states no exception or saving for the Council or its acts. Nothing shows any command of this order continuing after July 1, 1970.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date and no termination clause of its own. The earliest ending found is Executive Order 11541 section 2(b), effective July 1, 1970 (signing date July 1, 1970; its section 3 states the effective date). A held-text search for this order's number found no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument; Executive Order 11500 only amends section 1(c) and Executive Order 12553 came later.
scope_check: Fifteen clauses are inventoried by correction, covering the title and enacting clause with section 1(a), section 1(b) and (c), the section 2 lead and its eight numbered directions, section 3(a) and (b) and section 4. Executive Order 11541 terminates the Council as a whole, not in part. I read sections 3(b) and 4 as ending with the Council because they staff and constrain the Council and have no subject without it; that reading is disclosed.
independent_command_check: No command of this order operates apart from the Council: the composition, presiding, advisory functions, executive secretary, staff support and construction clause all depend on the body the order establishes. Executive Order 11541 section 2(b) provides that the functions heretofore assigned to the terminated organizations are performed by the Domestic Council, so the functions did not continue as commands of this order.
savings_check: Executive Order 11541 was read in full. research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12584 (52 FR 5429, PDF page 11 of the 1987-02-23 issue; sha256 9ce8d3b6...), headed "President’s Special Review Board" in the OCR layer, which splits many words with stray spaces. It is signed February 19, 1987, which matches the census register row (1987-02-19, President's Special Review Board). The machine heading search did not resolve the heading; I confirmed it by reading the OCR heading line, which reads Executive Order 12584 of February 19, 1987. Text and inventory: one operative paragraph; it extends the time within which the Board may submit its findings and recommendations by amending section 2(b) of Executive Order 12575 (as amended), deleting the date February 19, 1987 and inserting February 26, 1987. The inventory is one clause and I confirm it. Ending: Executive Order 12610 (signed 1987-09-30, effective that day) revokes Executive Order 12575, the parent that the amendment changes; the amended provision cannot operate without its parent. The amendment itself was made when signed, and its effect (the changed report date) lives in section 2(b) of the parent until the parent ends; that is the reading of the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, disclosed as a reading. The parent's own-terms sunset is a disclosed candidate earlier end and is not recorded as the end. Section 4 of Executive Order 12575 reads 'The Board shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report to the President.' A held Public Papers text (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12575_Date_the_President_s_Special_Review_Board_Tower_Commission_submitted_its_report_to_th_1875c02b67.txt, PPP-1987-book1 PDF pages 197-201; a held text lead from a scan's text layer, not an authenticated original) prints 'Remarks on Receiving the Final Report of the President’s Special Review Board on the National Security Council' dated February 26, 1987, so the report was received on that date, which is the date to which this order moved the report deadline, and 30 days after it is 1987-03-28. That sunset belongs to the parent's Board and is keyed to a report; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), applied here by disclosed analogy to a report-relative sunset, it is a spent fact and not an end of the order, which stays on the books until express revocation. No held source states that the Board was terminated on a date, apart from section 4 of the parent itself. Executive Order 12581 of January 28, 1987 (52 FR 2979) amended section 2(b) of Executive Order No. 12575 before this order and is an earlier amendment, not a later event; this order then deletes the date it set (February 19, 1987). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.
savings_reason: Executive Order 12610 revokes the parent order in section 3(g) with no saving wording in sections 1 through 5; the report-date extension served only the Board, which the order abolished, so nothing continues.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The parent order's own terms (section 4 of Executive Order 12575) end the Board 30 days after it submits its report; the extended report date of February 26, 1987 is a deadline, not an end, and the actual report is dated February 26, 1987 in a held Public Papers text, so the parent's own-terms sunset (the Board terminates 30 days after submitting its report, about 1987-03-28) is shown to have arisen, but it is a report-relative sunset treated as a spent fact and not an end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C, applied by disclosed analogy), and it is disclosed for the reviewer as a candidate earlier end. (2) Executive Order 12610 is the only held instrument after this order that names the parent (Executive Order 12581 of January 28, 1987 names section 2(b) of the parent but is an earlier amendment); a search of the held corpus for the number 12584 found no other instrument naming this order, and the OFR disposition-note machine search has no hit for it. (3) No instrument before 12610 revokes the parent.
scope_check: One clause. Executive Order 12610 section 3(g) revokes Executive Order 12575 in full, without any exception; it does not name Executive Order 12584, so the end rests on the parent being revoked, disclosed as a parent-as-amended reading. I read sections 1 through 5 of Executive Order 12610; section 4 supersedes Executive Order 12534 and does not bear on this order.
independent_command_check: The order has a single command, the amendment of the date in section 2(b) of Executive Order 12575. It gives no direction that outlives the parent order: its only effect is on the Board's report date.
savings_check: Executive Order 12610 sections 1 through 5 contain no wording that preserves Executive Order 12575 or its amendments: section 1 continues other committees, section 2 concerns only those, and section 3(g) revokes the parent without exception.
